report_title: Homeland Justice / Storm-0842 (DEV-0842) Actor Intelligence Pack — Stage-1 CTI Extraction
source: CISA/FBI Joint Cybersecurity Advisory AA22-264A 'Iranian State Actors Conduct Cyber Operations Against the Government of Albania', 2022-09-23 (https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa22-264a); Microsoft Threat Intelligence (MSTIC/DART) 'Microsoft investigates Iranian attacks against the Albanian government', 2022-09-08 (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/09/08/microsoft-investigates-iranian-attacks-against-the-albanian-government/); Mandiant 'ROADSWEEP Ransomware and CHIMNEYSWEEP Backdoor Deployed in Albania' reporting; Check Point Research 'Bad Karma, No Justice: Void Manticore Destructive Activities in Israel', 2024-05 (Void Manticore / Storm-0842 / Homeland Justice-Karma linkage). Behavioral chain (initial access via SharePoint CVE-2019-0604, ~14-month dwell, ROADSWEEP ransomware + No-Justice/NACL wiper deployment, defacement and leak via Telegram persona) is taken directly from AA22-264A; hashes and the CVE reproduced verbatim from the AA22-264A IOC tables.

actor.name: Homeland Justice
related_clusters: Scarred Manticore / Storm-0861 (adjacent MOIS-linked access-enabling cluster reported alongside)
Iran-Albania leak persona linked to Void Manticore (Storm-1084) and Scarred Manticore; tracked as its own pack for the Albania government operations.
actor.attribution: Iran-nexus destructive and hack-and-leak operation publicly assessed by CISA/FBI and Microsoft to be conducted by Iranian state cyber actors sponsored by the Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). 'Homeland Justice' is the public-facing persona (Telegram channel and leak website) used to claim, message, and leak stolen data following destructive intrusions. Microsoft tracks the destructive-operations actor as Storm-0842 (formerly DEV-0842); Check Point associates the Homeland Justice/Karma persona with the Void Manticore cluster. Attribution is a convergence of independent government and vendor reporting on the same July–September 2022 Albanian government intrusion; the specific tasking unit within MOIS is asserted at the ministry level, not a single named subordinate group. No MITRE ATT&CK G-id has been assigned.
targeted_sectors: Public services and critical government IT systems

key_campaigns.name: Destructive attack on the Government of Albania (ROADSWEEP + No-Justice wiper)
key_campaigns.date: Initial access ~May 2021; destructive attack July 15, 2022; follow-on Sept 2022
key_campaigns.summary: The actor gained initial access ~14 months prior by exploiting an internet-facing Microsoft SharePoint server (CVE-2019-0604), then maintained long dwell using .aspx web shells (ClientBin.aspx / App_Web_bckwssht.dll), RDP/VPN with compromised accounts, credential theft and lateral movement. In July 2022 it deployed the ROADSWEEP ransomware (GoXml.exe) launched via win.bat, changed desktop wallpaper with a Homeland Justice message, disabled Windows Defender (disable_defender.exe), deleted volume shadow copies (vssadmin), terminated processes (bb.bat taskkill loop), and separately wiped raw disks using cl.exe with the EldoS rwdsk.sys driver (a ZEROCLEARE-variant 'No-Justice'/NACL wiper). Stolen data was subsequently leaked and the intrusion publicized through the Homeland Justice Telegram persona and leak site. Follow-on activity against Albanian government systems continued in September 2022.

key_campaigns.name: Void Manticore / Homeland Justice-Karma destructive activity against Israel-linked targets
key_campaigns.summary: Check Point ties the Homeland Justice persona and the Karma leak brand to Void Manticore, a MOIS-linked destructive cluster conducting hack-and-leak and wiping operations against Israeli targets, sometimes handed access from a separate initial-access group (Scarred Manticore). Operations follow the same theft-then-destroy-then-publicize pattern, using custom wipers (BiBi wiper family in the Israel context), manual disk/partition corruption, and public leak personas for psychological impact.

malware: win.bat / bb.bat — batch launchers / process-kill scripts
tooling_observed: rwdsk.sys (EldoS RawDisk legitimate commercial driver, abused for raw disk access)

ttps.procedure_description: The actor operates the 'Homeland Justice' public persona — a Telegram channel and leak website — established to claim responsibility, message victims, and publish stolen Albanian government data. The Karma brand is used analogously in the Israel-context Void Manticore operations.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — off-victim persona and account creation are not visible in defender host/network logs; hunt candidate via external monitoring of leak sites/Telegram for early breach disclosure of owned data

ttps.procedure_description: Initial access ~14 months before the destructive attack was obtained by exploiting an internet-facing Microsoft SharePoint server via CVE-2019-0604, a .NET deserialization RCE in SharePoint.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — CVE-2019-0604 exploitation is detectable via SharePoint/IIS request patterns, WAF/IDS signatures, and vulnerable-version telemetry, though n-day exploitation of an exposed server may precede monitoring

ttps.procedure_description: Over the ~14-month dwell the actor repeatedly re-entered the environment using RDP and VPN access with compromised accounts, including logging in to a victim print server over RDP to stage the encryption component.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — authenticated remote access with valid credentials blends with legitimate use; hunt candidate via anomalous source-geo/ASN, off-hours logon, and new-account RDP/VPN correlation

ttps.procedure_description: The actor deployed .aspx web shells — ClientBin.aspx, which contains a Base64-encoded .NET executable (App_Web_bckwssht.dll) it decodes and loads — on the compromised SharePoint/IIS server to maintain access and proxy follow-on commands.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — new .aspx files in web-root paths and IIS worker (w3wp.exe) spawning child processes are strong web-shell signals, though a long-dormant shell may evade point-in-time review

ttps.procedure_description: The CHIMNEYSWEEP backdoor and follow-on tooling in the MOIS toolset establish persistence via scheduled tasks; Microsoft reporting on the Albania intrusion notes scheduled-task-based execution for maintaining foothold.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — scheduled-task creation (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational log) referencing unusual binaries or user-writable paths is detectable

ttps.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
ttps.procedure_description: win.bat was configured to launch the ROADSWEEP payload GoXml.exe (from C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\GoXml.exe) at system startup, ensuring the destructive component ran on boot.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — new startup/Run-key entries or Startup-folder scripts pointing at binaries in ProgramData are detectable via autostart and registry-write telemetry

ttps.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
ttps.procedure_description: The actor used batch scripts executed via cmd.exe — win.bat (#1 to run the malware, #2 to set the wallpaper) and bb.bat (a taskkill loop terminating a hardcoded process list) — to orchestrate the destructive stage.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — batch-driven cmd.exe issuing vssadmin/taskkill/reg-add commands in quick succession is a detectable destructive-staging pattern via process-command-line telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: Microsoft observed the actor using PowerShell and remote-execution tooling during the intrusion to run commands and move tooling across the Albanian government network.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — PowerShell script-block logging (4104) and AMSI telemetry detect follow-on command execution, though usage is easily blended with admin activity

ttps.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
ttps.procedure_description: The ClientBin.aspx web shell embeds a Base64-encoded .NET executable (App_Web_bckwssht.dll) which it decodes at runtime; the DLL in turn extracts a secondary Base64-encoded 'EncryptionDLL' (Base64.dll) loaded via Assembly.Load — layered encoding to hide the payload from static inspection.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — Base64-heavy .aspx content and large encoded blobs in web files are detectable via web-content inspection and entropy analysis

ttps.procedure_description: The web shell decodes its Base64-encoded .NET payload and dynamically loads it, and further decodes a secondary Base64 EncryptionDLL at runtime via Assembly.Load — runtime deobfuscation to defeat static detection.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — runtime decode-and-load behavior (Assembly.Load of decoded bytes) is detectable via .NET/CLR and script-block telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: The ROADSWEEP payload was staged as GoXml.exe under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\, placing the destructive binary in a Microsoft-looking directory path to blend with legitimate system content.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — path/name masquerading evades name-based rules; hunt candidate via unsigned/unknown executables in ProgramData\Microsoft paths and hash reputation

ttps.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
ttps.procedure_description: The actor ran disable_defender.exe, a PE that elevates and disables Windows Defender (manipulating Defender/SmartScreen via smartscreen.exe context) to clear the way for the ransomware and wiper without AV interference.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — Defender tamper events, service/registry changes disabling real-time protection, and execution of a known disable_defender binary are detectable via EDR tamper-protection and Defender operational logs

ttps.procedure_description: win.bat (#2) writes the HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\Wallpaper registry value to point at a Homeland Justice message image (goxml.jpg) and forces a per-user parameter refresh via RUNDLL32 user32.dll,UpdatePerUserSystemParameters.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — scripted registry writes to the Wallpaper value followed by a forced desktop refresh across many hosts is an anomalous, detectable pattern

ttps.procedure_description: Microsoft observed credential theft during the intrusion, enabling the actor to obtain and reuse valid accounts for RDP/VPN access and lateral movement across the Albanian government network over the long dwell time.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — LSASS access, SAM/registry-hive dumping, and credential-theft tooling are detectable via process-access (Sysmon EID 10) and command-line telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: Microsoft reporting notes network scanning during the intrusion (e.g. Advanced Port Scanner) to enumerate reachable hosts and services ahead of lateral movement and the destructive stage.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — internal horizontal port-scan connection fan-out and known scanner-binary execution are detectable, though scan tools are easily renamed

ttps.procedure_description: The actor enumerated remote hosts across the government network to identify servers (print server, database and file servers) targeted for encryption and wiping during the long pre-attack dwell.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — host-enumeration bursts across a subnet are detectable but blend with legitimate administration

ttps.procedure_description: The ROADSWEEP encryption component enumerates files and directories on target hosts to select content for encryption, and the wiper enumerates volumes/files for destruction.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — file enumeration is ubiquitous and low-signal on its own; hunt candidate only in correlation with the subsequent encrypt/wipe burst

ttps.procedure_description: For the encryption stage the actor logged in to a victim organization print server via RDP and used it as a distribution point, and used RDP with compromised accounts to move laterally to targeted servers.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — RDP from atypical internal hosts (e.g. a print server originating outbound RDP) and lateral-RDP graph anomalies are detectable via logon (4624 type 10) analytics

ttps.procedure_description: The actor staged and distributed the destructive payloads to multiple hosts from a central server (using the print server as a distribution point), consistent with SMB/admin-share-based spreading of GoXml.exe and the batch scripts before mass execution.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — payload copies to ADMIN$/C$ shares followed by remote execution across many hosts are detectable via SMB write and remote-create telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: The actor transferred the destructive tooling (GoXml.exe, cl.exe, win.bat, bb.bat, disable_defender.exe) from the compromised distribution host to target machines across the network prior to detonating the encryption and wipe.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — executable/script copies between internal hosts shortly before execution are detectable via file-write and network-share telemetry

ttps.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
ttps.procedure_description: The No-Justice wiper (cl.exe) loads rwdsk.sys, a legitimate EldoS Corporation RawDisk commercial driver, installed/loaded as a kernel service to obtain raw block-level access to the hard drive for wiping (bring-your-own-vulnerable/abusable-driver).
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — installation/load of the EldoS RawDisk driver (rwdsk.sys) and new kernel-service creation (Event ID 7045 / Sysmon driver-load EID 6) are detectable, and the driver hash is a known IOC

ttps.procedure_description: Prior to the destructive stage the actor collected sensitive Albanian government data from compromised systems, which was later leaked publicly through the Homeland Justice persona as part of the hack-and-leak operation.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — bulk local file access is high-volume normal activity; hunt candidate via large-scale read/stage sequences preceding exfiltration

ttps.procedure_description: Stolen government data was aggregated and archived for staged public release across successive Homeland Justice Telegram/leak-site postings, consistent with archiving collected data prior to exfiltration.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — archiving utilities are common admin tools; hunt candidate via large archive creation over staged directories preceding outbound transfer

ttps.procedure_description: The ClientBin.aspx / App_Web_bckwssht.dll web shell accepts HTTP POST requests carrying a Base64-encoded IP and port and opens a second socket to the supplied address — a web-protocol-fronted command-and-control / relay channel.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — POST requests to an unusual .aspx endpoint followed by the web server initiating outbound sockets to arbitrary IP:port is a detectable web-shell C2 pattern

ttps.procedure_description: Follow-on tooling and destructive payloads were brought into the environment over the long dwell via the web shell and remote-access channels for staging before the July 2022 attack.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — the web server or a beaconing host writing new executables to disk shortly after inbound C2 is detectable via network-to-file-create correlation

ttps.procedure_description: The web shell's socket-relay capability (open a second socket to an attacker-supplied IP:port) provided a channel to move stolen government data out of the environment for later publication via the Homeland Justice persona.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — exfil folded into web-shell C2 sockets blends with server traffic; hunt candidate via anomalous large outbound transfers from a web/SharePoint server

ttps.procedure_description: Before encryption, bb.bat runs a taskkill loop (@for %C in (%PrcLst%) do @taskkill /f /im "%C.exe") to force-terminate a hardcoded list of processes — unlocking database/application files so the ROADSWEEP encryptor can access and encrypt them.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — a scripted taskkill /f loop against a broad process list immediately before mass file changes is a high-value, detectable ransomware/wiper precursor

ttps.procedure_description: The destructive script executes @vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet to delete all Volume Shadow Copies, preventing restoration before the ransomware/wiper renders systems unrecoverable.
ttps.detection_feasibility: high — vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet is a discrete, high-fidelity, well-covered destructive precursor and one of the most reliable early-warning signals

ttps.procedure_description: The ROADSWEEP ransomware (GoXml.exe), launched by win.bat with the arguments '1 2 3 4 5 6 7', encrypts files on targeted hosts and drops a ransom/message note as part of the destructive operation against the Albanian government.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — by the time high-rate encryption is observable the impact is occurring; hunt/detect the precursors (vssadmin, taskkill, Defender disable, web-shell). File-entropy/canary analytics can catch it mid-run but recovery may already be lost

ttps.procedure_description: Separately from the encryption, the actor deployed cl.exe (the 'No-Justice' / NACL wiper, a ZEROCLEARE variant) which uses the EldoS rwdsk.sys driver to obtain raw disk access and destroy data, rendering victim systems unusable.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — mass raw-disk destruction is concurrent with impact; hunt/detect via the precursor driver load (rwdsk.sys) and raw-device handle acquisition rather than the wipe itself

ttps.procedure_description: cl.exe is part of a disk-wiper utility that provides raw access to the hard drive (via the EldoS RawDisk driver) for the express purpose of overwriting/wiping data content on the physical disk.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — a user-mode process acquiring a raw \\.\PhysicalDrive handle via the EldoS driver and issuing large sequential writes is a rare, high-fidelity destructive signal via disk-I/O/raw-handle telemetry

ttps.procedure_description: As a ZEROCLEARE-lineage wiper, the No-Justice tooling corrupts disk structures (boot sector / partition data) through raw disk access to prevent the system from booting, in addition to destroying file content.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — raw writes to the boot sector / first physical sectors via the RawDisk driver are a rare, high-fidelity destructive signal, though concurrent with the impact

ttps.procedure_description: win.bat (#2) sets the desktop wallpaper on victim hosts to a Homeland Justice message image (goxml.jpg), an internal defacement delivering the actor's political messaging directly on compromised endpoints.
ttps.detection_feasibility: medium — scripted mass wallpaper/registry changes to a dropped image across many hosts is a detectable, anomalous internal-defacement pattern

ttps.procedure_description: Following the destruction, the actor publicized the intrusion and leaked stolen Albanian government data through the external Homeland Justice Telegram channel and leak website, using public messaging/defacement for psychological and political impact.
ttps.detection_feasibility: low — external leak/messaging occurs off-victim; hunt candidate via external/brand and leak-site monitoring for early disclosure of owned data

detection_signals: SharePoint/IIS request patterns consistent with CVE-2019-0604 (.NET deserialization RCE) against an internet-facing SharePoint server, followed by new .aspx files (ClientBin.aspx) in the web root

Base64-heavy .aspx web shell content that decodes and Assembly.Load's an embedded .NET DLL (App_Web_bckwssht.dll / Base64.dll), and the web server opening outbound sockets to an attacker-supplied IP:port after a POST
Execution of disable_defender.exe or Defender tamper events disabling real-time protection immediately before mass file activity
@vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet — shadow-copy deletion (high-fidelity wiper/ransomware precursor)
bb.bat-style scripted taskkill /f /im loop terminating a broad hardcoded process list right before file encryption

win.bat launching GoXml.exe from C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\ at startup, plus a Wallpaper registry write to goxml.jpg followed by RUNDLL32 user32.dll,UpdatePerUserSystemParameters across many hosts
Load/installation of the EldoS RawDisk driver rwdsk.sys and a user-mode process (cl.exe) acquiring a raw \\.\PhysicalDrive handle for block-level writes — No-Justice/ZEROCLEARE wipe
RDP originating from an internal print/file server used as a payload distribution point, and lateral payload copies (GoXml.exe/cl.exe/win.bat) to multiple hosts before synchronized detonation
Long-dwell reuse of compromised accounts over RDP/VPN with anomalous source geo/ASN across a ~14-month window
External monitoring: appearance of organizational data or claims on the Homeland Justice / Karma Telegram channel or leak site (post-impact confirmation and, for peers, early-warning)
notes: Actor has NO MITRE ATT&CK G-id; mitre_id left empty per schema. 'Homeland Justice' is the persona/leak brand for an MOIS-sponsored destructive operation Microsoft tracks as Storm-0842/DEV-0842 and Check Point associates with the Void Manticore / Karma cluster. The behavioral chain and all IOCs are drawn from CISA/FBI AA22-264A (fetched via browser-UA curl after an initial 403), enriched with Microsoft MSTIC and Check Point reporting for named tooling (CHIMNEYSWEEP backdoor, PowerShell, credential dumping, port scanning) that AA22-264A does not itself hash. FRAMEWORK-VERSION CONVENTIONS honored for this environment's bundled dataset: Impair-Defenses = T1685 under tactic 'defense-impairment' (NOT legacy T1562.*); defense-evasion tactic slug = 'stealth' (used for T1027.013, T1140, T1036, T1112); encrypted/encoded file = T1027.013. Every technique_id was verified present in this env's sigma.data.mitre_attack.mitre_attack_techniques before inclusion; no invalid IDs were emitted (none dropped). 33 techniques across 11 tactics. IMPACT is the payload cluster (8 techniques): T1489 Service Stop (bb.bat taskkill), T1490 Inhibit System Recovery (vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet), T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact (ROADSWEEP GoXml.exe), T1485 Data Destruction (cl.exe No-Justice wiper), T1561.001 Disk Content Wipe + T1561.002 Disk Structure Wipe (EldoS rwdsk.sys raw-disk / ZEROCLEARE lineage), T1491.001 Internal Defacement (wallpaper), T1491.002 External Defacement (Telegram/leak site). DETECTION-vs-HUNT: the highest-value early-warning DETECTIONS fire before/at destruction — T1490 (vssadmin), T1685 (Defender disable), T1489 (taskkill loop), T1505.003 (web shell), T1543.003 (rwdsk.sys driver load) — these define the practical containment window. The encrypt/wipe acts themselves (T1486/T1485/T1561.*) are marked LOW/route-to-hunt because by the time they are observable, impact is occurring; the off-victim persona/leak activity (T1585.001, T1491.002, T1005/T1560/T1041 exfil) is HUNT via external monitoring. IOCs are verbatim from the AA22-264A IOC tables: CVE-2019-0604 (SharePoint initial access), 10 SHA-256 and 19 MD5 file hashes covering GoXml.exe (ROADSWEEP), cl.exe (No-Justice wiper) + rwdsk.sys, ClientBin.aspx / App_Web_bckwssht.dll web shell, disable_defender.exe, win.bat/bb.bat, and goxml.jpg. No malicious IPs, domains, or emails were published in AA22-264A (the only IP-like token in the page was the '1.0.0.0' assembly version string and CISA's own contact address — both excluded, not fabricated), so those arrays are intentionally empty. No verbatim YARA rule appeared in the fetched source, so yara_rules is empty (never authored from scratch). IOCs (esp. hashes) expire fast; the TTPs and detection_signals are the durable pipeline value.
